headline: Recovery update covers housing gap and water system purchase

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.summary: The committee heard updates on Maui's long-term recovery, housing, and a proposed water system purchase, and met in closed session.
meeting.recap: The county has committed $1.278 billion of its $1.6 billion in recovery funds.[[0:15:49]] More than 1,100 households are still in temporary housing.[[0:18:28]] The county will take over the disaster case management program from the state in August.[[0:19:16]] A new rental help program, the Disaster Interim Housing Program, starts in August.[[0:22:05]] The county is proposing to buy a private irrigation company's non-potable (not for drinking) water system.[[0:28:48]] The county wants about $2.9 million in improvements to that system after the sale closes.[[0:30:30]] The state's temporary housing site, now housing 960 people, runs through August 2029.[[0:37:15]] The state said the case management program has closed 898 cases, meaning those households reached their recovery goals.[[0:41:40]] A water coalition testifier said Lahaina already uses at least 90 percent of its sustainable water supply.[[1:10:20]] The chair said the water and land purchase must be discussed privately due to a nondisclosure agreement.[[1:27:50]] Members voted 7–0 to go into executive session (a closed-door discussion).[[1:39:16]] The housing director said he would look into a mold complaint at Haleʻola.[[1:43:12]]

moments.q: This week marks the three-year anniversary of the August 2023 wildfires.
What are we going to do with the 960 or 1000 plus individuals
We are at least at 90 percent of sustainable yield
Vote to enter executive session: 7 ayes, 0 nos

issues.oneLine: The county is proposing to buy a private irrigation company's non-potable water system.
issues.why: A water coalition testifier said Lahaina already uses at least 90 percent of its sustainable water supply.
issues.brief: The system has two stream diversions, two shaft wells, one well, and three reservoirs.[[#1]] The county is requesting about $2.9 million in improvements after the sale closes.[[#2]] A testifier said water source has held up shovel-ready housing projects in West Maui.[[#3]]
